module_title: Introduction to the Cell and Basic Types
introduction: The Cell is the fundamental 'structural and functional unit' of life. Just as bricks are the building blocks of a house, cells are the building blocks of all living organisms. Cytology is the branch of science that deals with the study of cells.

core_concepts.title: Discovery of the Cell
core_concepts.description:
1. Robert Hooke (1665): He was the first to discover a cell. He observed a thin slice of cork under a microscope and saw honeycomb-like structures. Note: He discovered a 'Dead Cell'. 
2. Antonie van Leeuwenhoek (1674): He was the first to discover and observe 'Free-living Cells' (like bacteria and protozoa) in pond water.

core_concepts.title: The Cell Theory
core_concepts.description:
Proposed by Schleiden (Botanist) and Schwann (Zoologist) in 1838-39. 
Postulates: 
1. All living organisms are composed of cells. 
2. The cell is the basic unit of life. 
Later, Rudolf Virchow (1855) expanded it with the famous phrase: 'Omnis cellula-e-cellula', meaning 'All new cells arise from pre-existing cells'.

core_concepts.title: Types of Cells: Prokaryotic vs. Eukaryotic
core_concepts.description:
1. Prokaryotic Cells: Primitive and underdeveloped. They lack a well-defined 'Nucleus' (their genetic material floats freely) and have no membrane-bound organelles. Examples: Bacteria, Blue-green algae (Cyanobacteria). 
2. Eukaryotic Cells: Advanced and fully developed. They have a distinct, membrane-bound Nucleus and all membrane-bound organelles. Examples: Plants, Animals, Fungi.

core_concepts.title: Plant Cell vs. Animal Cell
core_concepts.description:
1. Plant Cell: Possesses a rigid 'Cell Wall', contains 'Plastids' (like Chloroplast for photosynthesis), and has a very large central vacuole that pushes the nucleus to the side. 
2. Animal Cell: Lacks a cell wall and plastids. Contains 'Centrosomes' (centrioles) which help in cell division, a feature absent in higher plant cells.

important_entities.name: Composition of the Cell Wall
important_entities.significance:
A highly tested fact in exams: 
- The cell wall of Plants is made of 'Cellulose'. 
- The cell wall of Fungi is made of 'Chitin'. 
- The cell wall of Bacteria is made of 'Peptidoglycan'.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: Do viruses follow the Cell Theory? Answer: NO! Viruses are 'Acellular' (not composed of cells). They are considered the connecting link between living and non-living things because they are dead outside a host body but become alive and multiply inside it.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Hooke found a Dead Cork; Leeuwen-Hawk (Hawk-eye) spotted the Live ones.
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Robert Hooke discovered the dead cork cell. Antonie van Leeuwenhoek (sounds like Hawk) used his sharp lenses to find living cells.

exam_strategy_tips: A direct and permanent question in SSC exams: 'What is the structural and functional unit of life?' Answer: The Cell.
